title: Accessibility
goal: Make a small page work with keyboard and assistive technology.
explanation: Semantic HTML provides many useful behaviours by default. Use a button for an action and a link for navigation. Every form control needs an accessible name.

Try the whole page with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space as appropriate. Focus must remain visible and in a sensible order. An image needs alternative text based on its purpose; decorative images can have empty alt text.

WCAG AA contrast for ordinary text is at least 4.5:1, with 3:1 for large text under the standard definition. Automated checks catch only some issues; include manual keyboard and screen-reader testing.
exercise: Test your contact form without a mouse. Record and fix one unclear label or focus problem.
hint: Do not remove outlines without providing a clearly visible replacement.

quiz.question: Which control is the best starting point for a keyboard-accessible action?
quiz.explanation: A native button already supports focus and standard keyboard activation.
